author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text: We almost reach the point LLM is no longer AI.

reshared_post.author_headline: AI Engineer | C#/.NET · LLM Integration | App Modernization
reshared_post.reshared_text:
AI is whatever we haven’t automated yet.

In the 1960s, recognizing handwritten text was “artificial intelligence.”
In the 1980s, beating a chess grandmaster was “artificial intelligence.”
In the 2000s, speech recognition was “artificial intelligence.”
Today, all of that is “just software.”

The line between “AI” and “ordinary computing” isn’t technical — it’s cultural.

Once something works reliably, we stop calling it AI and start calling it “an app,” “a feature,” or “productivity software.”
